title: Code quality: formatting, linting, and tests

questions.prompt: Which tool checks runtime behavior for selected input cases?
questions.explanation: Tests execute selected cases and compare observed behavior with expected results.

questions.prompt: What does a formatter primarily do?
options: Proves the program has no bugs.
Runs the program against a database.
Changes Python values into type annotations.
questions.explanation: Formatters standardize layout; they do not replace behavioral tests.

questions.prompt: Why control time, randomness, and external services in tests where practical?
options: To make results more repeatable and easier to diagnose.
To prevent tests from checking edge cases.
To ensure every test passes without assertions.
questions.answer: To make results more repeatable and easier to diagnose.
questions.explanation: Reducing uncontrolled inputs helps tests remain deterministic.
